findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The facility could not produce any food manager certificates. The only Certified Food Manager on file wasn’t available during the visit. PIC mentioned that the certificates were locked in the office room and the employees did not have a key to access the documents at the time of the inspection. Ensure that there is always a certified food protection manager present during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: The employee who normally handles food was observed processing transactions at the register and engaging in food prep without washing hands. Discussed with PIC the need to wash hands before handling food since there was an interruption of tasks. Ensure that employees wash hands in between changing tasks to avoid cross contaminating food.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: The PIC mentioned that employees normally wash hands in the ware-washing sink where dishes are cleaned. Discussed with PIC that handwashing should only occur in the handwashing sink. The triple sink shall only be used for cleaning dishes. Ensure that hands are washed in the designated hand sink only.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.15 Where to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source.
findings.comment: The facility is serving yogurt dipped grapes. When asked the source of the grapes, the PIC wasn’t aware of where the grapes are being made. Discussed that food sold for public consumption must be made in an approved permitted kitchen. The facility was instructed to not serve the grapes to the public. Will follow-up on November 24, 2025 to gather more information about the food source.
findings.citation_text: 3-201.11(A) Compliance with Food Law. (A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There are several missing ceiling tiles in the back storage area where single service items, bottled drinks, and the ice machine are stored. PIC was able to replace one ceiling tile, however, the facility is still expected to replace the remaining missing tiles. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The top inside surface of the ice machine was observed to be heavily soiled with mold. PIC stated that the machine will be serviced and cleaned as soon as possible. Ensure that food-contact surfaces of the ice machine are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent accumulation and possible contamination of food. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the baffles of the ice machine to have mold accumulation. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that baffles are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent mold accumulation and possible contamination. Will follow-up on 12/2/2024. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: There wasn't a sanitizer solution present at the start of the inspection. Discussed with PIC and sanitizer solution was created and tested at 200ppm. Be sure sanitizer solutions are available during food preparation to ensure that food contact surfaces are properly getting sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 
(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
The individual who was handling food during the inspection isn’t food handler certified. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that employees who are not Food Manager certified are food handler certified if handling or preparing food.

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed deli meats in the reach in cooler to be probed at internal temperatures of 52F. These were just sliced this morning and the mayo in the bottom portion of this cooler is 43F.  In my history with this facility, the cooler is always <41F in the mornings, but during lunch when they are in and out of the cooler, temperature abuse is occurring because this type of cooler is not neccessarily designed for what it is being used for. In an hour, the temperature will be <41F again. All meats, cheeses, tomatoes and other PHF that will not be used within 4 hours were moved to the walk in cooler during the inspection, which is holding at 36F. Only keep what you will use within 4 hours in this cooler until the new unit arrives.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) .

NEW>3) There is splatter of a red/brown substance above the bagged ice freezer. Clean the ceiling. 4) The ceiling tiles above the sandwich prep area are acoustic. 750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
750-1210(b) Walls and ceilings in walk-in refrigeration units, food prepartion areas, equipment washing areas, and toilet rooms shall be smooth, light-cored, non-absorbant, and easily cleanable. Concrete or pumice block in these locations shall be finished and sealed to provide a cleanable surface.

findings.title: Rooms and equipment - vented as required
findings.comment:
The vent in the restroom does not appear to be working at this time. Facility believes it is working, but vent is not audible to inspectors. Repair vent to provide properly vented restrooms.
750-1250 All rooms shall have sufficient ventilation to keep them free of excessive, heat, steam, condensation, vapors, obnoxious odors, smoke, and fumes. Provide adequate ventilation.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed Raid, d-Con (rat bait) and flat tire repair stored aboved toothpaste and toothbrushes on retail shelves. Store items for human consumption above any chemicals and toxic sibstances.
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: CORRECTED> Observed an unapproved hand sanitizer next to the hand sink in the sandwich prep area. Hand sanitizer was removed.
findings.citation_text: 750.1320 Bactericides intended for use on food contact surfaces should not be used in a way that leaves a toxic residue on such surfaces.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment: 1)There is a display cooler in the retail aisles and a 2 door Traulsen cooler in the back that are not in use. Remove all unneccessary items. 2) Mop head was stored in dirty mop water. Hand or invert mop to dry and dispose of dirty mop water after use. 750-1350c Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.  Remove all unnecessary items. 750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similiar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food. 750-1160 The premises shall be kept in such a condition to prevent the harborage or feeding of insects or rodents.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
CORRECTED > Was informed by an employee that he washes his hands in the three part sink as opposed to the installed hand sink. Discussed with facility that hands must not be washed in a three pan dish sink.
750-1120c Sinks used for food preparation or for washing equipment or utensils shall not be used for hand washing.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1) Observed the lid over the soda machine self serve ice to be missing the corner. repair or replace lid so ice is properly protected. 2) observed several shelves in the front counter area to have chipped edges showing the bare particle board. Seal all bare wood. 3) Observed the back display freezer to have ice accumulation. Defrost freezer.
750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
No Chlorine test strips were provided to test the concentration of the sanitizer. Provide test strips.
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1)REPEAT >  the soda nozzles on the self serve soda machine. 2) REPEAT > The interior of the microwave. 3) 2ND REPEAT > The coffee maker spout. 4) REPEAT > The interior cabinets of the cappuccino machines. 5) 2ND REPEAT > The interior of the ice machine. Clean all food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) The interior of the display freezers. 2) The tops of all equipment on the self serve counter along with the counter itself under and behind equipment. 3) 2ND REPEAT > The cabinets below the self serve counter. 4) The Shelves behind the cappuccino machines. 5) The soda machine pumping equipment. 6) the shelving in the walk-in cooler and dry storage areas. Clean all non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed utensils and dishes being stored in soiled drawers and on soiled shelves. Store all clean utensils in a clean and dry place protected.
750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
1) Observed coffee filters being stored on top of the coffee maker unprotected. Store coffee filters in a clean container covered. 2) Observed to-go cups being stored on the floor in the back storage area. Store cups 6 inches off the ground.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
No soap was observed at the hand sink. Provide hand soap at the hand sink. 2) REPEAT > No self closer was observed on the restroom door.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1) 2ND REPEAT > Observed the floors through out the facility to be soiled along the walls and under and behind equipment. Clean the floors. 2) REPEAT > Observed the floor to be missing tiles in several areas. Repair floor so it is smooth and easily cleanable. 3) Observed coving to be missing or peeling away from wall throughout the back storage areas. Reseal existing coving to the wall and replace missing coving.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.
